title: An open ledger of computational progress
subtitle: What we have made executable, what the evidence actually establishes, and the work that remains between a promising compiler and a serious scientific instrument.

methodology.name: Verified acceptance gates
methodology.text: Each workstream is a set of explicitly weighted acceptance gates totalling 100 points. A gate contributes its full weight only when marked verified and linked to source or reproducible evidence. In-progress and planned work contribute zero. Workstream percentages are the sum of verified gate weights; the portfolio percentage is a weighted average across workstreams.
methodology.caveat: These percentages describe completion of the published acceptance plan—not research certainty, elapsed time, engineering difficulty, production readiness, or an industry-wide benchmark. Criteria and weights are editorial choices, versioned in Git; new requirements may change percentages.
methodology.refresh: This is a versioned public snapshot, not a live monitor. It updates when the roadmap data is reviewed, merged, and the site deploys. For the latest underlying code, inspect the linked repository and CI.

workstreams.title: Collaborative research workbench
workstreams.summary: The browser should become a place where several minds can examine one computation without losing its mathematical structure.
workstreams.impact: Shared exploration turns an algorithm from an isolated developer artifact into an object researchers can jointly investigate.
workstreams.now: Graph interaction, Yjs collaboration, bounded FX analysis and compiler evidence inspection exist.
workstreams.next: Connect the evidence ledger to richer graph inspection; independently audit accessibility and real-world collaborative usability.

criteria.title: Interactive graph and tensor inspection
criteria.why: React Flow diagrams, tensor metadata and three-dimensional previews are implemented.

criteria.title: Collaborative state and presence
criteria.why: Yjs synchronizes document state and collaborative presence.

criteria.title: Trusted FX analysis
criteria.why: Admitted model examples can be represented and examined through the local Python backend.

criteria.title: Live typed IR inspection
criteria.why: The Atlas can display a bounded, independently checked semantic decoder witness.

criteria.title: Unified research and evidence studio
criteria.why: Bring typed operations, model identity, measurements and provenance into one navigable research surface.

criteria.title: Independent accessibility and usability audit
criteria.why: Verify keyboard navigation, screen-reader semantics and collaboration with real users.

workstreams.title: Executable semantic representation
workstreams.summary: Optimization only deserves to be trusted when the system can distinguish what a program means from how it happens to run.
workstreams.impact: An explicit semantic boundary allows transformations to be inspected, rejected or reused across implementations.
workstreams.now: Typed operations, state ordering, graph-driven decoder math and checkpoint binding have independent tests.
workstreams.next: Generalize the operator and effect contract to genuinely different pretrained architectures.

criteria.title: Typed tensors and SSA operations
criteria.why: The SemanticProgram represents typed values, regions and operations.

criteria.title: Transactional state effects
criteria.why: KV writes, snapshots, failures and atomic cursor publication are exercised.

criteria.title: Graph-driven mathematical execution
criteria.why: The bounded decoder executes arithmetic from declared operations.

criteria.title: Checkpoint-bound canonical admission
criteria.why: Model tensors and graph identity are checked before execution.

criteria.title: At least two independent pretrained families
criteria.why: One Llama-specific success does not establish a universal compiler.

workstreams.title: Real-model and tokenizer fidelity
workstreams.summary: A compiler matters only when it can preserve the behavior of real learned systems, including their inconvenient details.
workstreams.impact: Real checkpoint fidelity bridges elegant intermediate representations with scientific reproducibility.
workstreams.now: The pinned Tiny Llama checkpoint, tokenizer witnesses, KV decode and canonical bundle have been exercised.
workstreams.next: Add another independently certified family and expand adversarial real-model coverage.

criteria.title: Real pinned safetensors checkpoint
criteria.why: A named model revision and file hashes have independent numerical witnesses.

criteria.title: Tokenizer-to-model agreement
criteria.why: Two explicit text witnesses match the reference tokenizer and logits.

criteria.title: Incremental stateful decoding
criteria.why: Chunked logits and KV states match independent references for admitted contexts.

criteria.title: Checkpoint-bound executable bundle
criteria.why: Strict reload refuses modified or unauthorized graphs.

criteria.title: Additional pretrained architecture family
criteria.why: Support must include the actual operator dialect, tokenizer, weights and state semantics.

workstreams.title: Independent compilation and hardware
workstreams.summary: A compiler becomes useful across machines when its semantics can survive translation into different physical execution systems.
workstreams.impact: Native compilation and hardware calibration determine whether this work can become a genuine hardware-algorithm co-design platform.
workstreams.now: Reference NumPy and complete CPU TorchScript execution are verified. Independent C++ lowering is underway, not yet certified.
workstreams.next: Certify a truly independent native CPU implementation, then build a competitive GPU backend and portable compiled artifacts.

criteria.title: Independent NumPy and PyTorch references
criteria.why: A different implementation supplies finite numerical witnesses.

criteria.title: Whole-decoder TorchScript execution
criteria.why: A complete decoder was traced and compared against a pinned model.

criteria.title: Independently generated native C++ CPU kernel
criteria.why: A native backend must execute the admitted mathematics without delegating computation to PyTorch or NumPy, then pass numerical/KV tests.

criteria.title: Independent GPU execution
criteria.why: CUDA/Triton/IREE or another real device path must be measured, not merely simulated.

criteria.title: Portable offline native compiled artifact
criteria.why: Loadable binaries require provenance, compatibility and cross-process validation.

workstreams.title: Search, fusion and execution economics
workstreams.summary: The objective is not one fast kernel. It is the ability to explain why one implementation is better, and under which constraints.
workstreams.impact: Source-bound measurements let us promote beneficial transformations while retaining the failures that teach us.
workstreams.now: Fused FFN, live-prefix KV, compile-once templates and matched small CPU benchmarks have been measured.
workstreams.next: Extend from tiny CPU experiments to long-context prefill/decode, throughput, latency tails and actual memory costs.

criteria.title: Verified operator fusion
criteria.why: A pure SwiGLU region matched an independent reference and reduced dispatch overhead.

criteria.title: Dynamic live-prefix KV execution
criteria.why: One graph handles varying positions and emits only new K/V suffixes.

criteria.title: Compile-once and weight reuse
criteria.why: Graph and weight modules are reused across private sessions with cold-start measurements.

criteria.title: Source-bound comparative CPU benchmark
criteria.why: Source hashes, versions and distinct warm/cold measurements are retained.

criteria.title: Representative serving and long-context benchmarks
criteria.why: Current tiny CPU tests cannot establish competitive serving economics.

workstreams.title: Evidence, provenance and safety
workstreams.summary: An optimization should be an argument supported by evidence, not merely a claim made by its author.
workstreams.impact: Transparent methods turn compiler results into accumulated research knowledge rather than disconnected demonstrations.
workstreams.now: Hash-bound experiments, negative tests, independent logits, benchmark JSON and CI exist.
workstreams.next: Expand across machines, input distributions and truly independent deployment targets.

criteria.title: Independent numerical oracles
criteria.why: NumPy, eager PyTorch and HF witnesses compare admitted outputs.

criteria.title: Content-bound checkpoint provenance
criteria.why: Exact model revision and file hashes are recorded, with authentication limits stated.

criteria.title: Inspectable reproducible benchmark records
criteria.why: Source-bound JSON records include scope, metrics and limitations.

criteria.title: Failure and tampering tests
criteria.why: Malformed graphs, cache writes, quota failures and eviction have negative coverage.

criteria.title: Reproduced physical results across independent machines
criteria.why: One CI runner and finite witnesses are not a cross-machine certification.

workstreams.title: Shared execution and resource ownership
workstreams.summary: A useful execution platform must know who owns computation and state, and what survives a failure or eviction.
workstreams.impact: Explicit model and session lifetimes are prerequisites for reliable multi-user research infrastructure.
workstreams.now: LRU model ownership, KV leases and active model-module counting are implemented.
workstreams.next: Measure and constrain physical resource usage in isolated workers before hosting untrusted requests.

criteria.title: Bounded model-template LRU
criteria.why: Verified semantic fingerprints govern cache admission, hits and eviction.

criteria.title: Private KV leases and release
criteria.why: Logical quota rejection and deterministic close have tested contracts.

criteria.title: Evicted-but-live model lifetime
criteria.why: Active modules remain accounted for until final lease release.

criteria.title: Measured physical RSS/resource enforcement
criteria.why: Logical byte budgets do not bound native heap or process RSS.

criteria.title: Hardened multi-tenant isolation and cancellation
criteria.why: Untrusted Python must run under a separate enforceable security boundary.

workstreams.title: Hardware–algorithm co-design
workstreams.summary: Physical machines impose their own logic: precision, calibration, conversion, memory and energy.
workstreams.impact: Hardware-aware algorithm design becomes credible only when simulated advantages survive measurement.
workstreams.now: Optical and heterogeneous placement hypotheses can be explored in software.
workstreams.next: Connect the cost models to calibrated device measurements and an actual independently executing accelerator.

criteria.title: Modeled optical operations and noise
criteria.why: The simulator exercises bounded hypothetical optical transfer/noise semantics.

criteria.title: Hypothetical heterogeneous placement
criteria.why: Placement explores declared abstract cost units, not measured latency.

criteria.title: Calibrated hardware cost models
criteria.why: Measurements from physical hardware must replace unvalidated assumptions.

criteria.title: Validated accelerator end-to-end execution
criteria.why: No physical photonic inference has been demonstrated.
